artifacts.summary: Confirms (via live reproduction against BimodalLogic) the --regenerate silent crash at covered_ids_from()'s unguarded grep-under-pipefail, finds --prune silently exits 0 while destroying ~280 lines of content on the same fixture, confirms --print and the deprecated script copy are unaffected, and flags the fixture's own self-declared 'hand-curated, not mechanically parsed' / 'superseded' status plus observed header drift as evidence for the planner's scope decision on how much of the stage layout to structurally round-trip.

memory_candidates.content: bash pipefail gotcha: a pipeline assigned to a variable via a bare (non-local) command substitution, e.g. var="$(a | b | c)", is NOT exempted by set -e's usual if/while/&&/||/! carve-outs. Under set -euo pipefail, if any stage of the pipe fails (e.g. a leading `grep` with no match, exit 1) and pipefail makes the whole pipeline's exit status non-zero, the shell exits immediately once the assignment completes -- even though the variable DOES get assigned its (possibly correct-looking, e.g. empty-array '[]') value first. A `bash -x` trace shows the assignment line printed right before the process dies. Audit for this shape anywhere a grep/jq pipeline with a possible no-match leading stage feeds a plain variable assignment under set -euo pipefail; the fix is `|| true`/`|| :` on the pipeline, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the same file for an analogous case.

A generator script with a hardcoded closed-vocabulary section grammar (fixed ## header literals for extraction AND reassembly) can silently treat 'none of my headers matched' as 'this file has nothing in those sections' rather than as an error -- and depending on which code path, this manifests as either a crash (an unguarded pipe choking on empty input) or, more dangerously, a clean exit-0 run that overwrites the whole file with an empty fixed template. When auditing or designing such a generator, always test the all-headers-absent case explicitly for BOTH exit code and diff/content effect -- a crash-free mode is not evidence of safety.
